title: Manifest
description: Response body of GET {extranet}/monitoring/manifest. The hub's declaration of what this tenant wants checked. Pulled by the prober on boot, on a slow reconcile schedule, and after a change notice. Also serves as the prober's 'can I reach this extranet' heartbeat.

tenant.description: Tenant slug. Must match the key the prober has in its own tenant config.

id.description: An id owned by the hub. Serialised as a string on the wire even when the hub stores it as an integer.

token.description: URL-safe secret placed in a path segment.

hibernates.description: The site sleeps between requests, so every check wakes it. The prober enforces a 60-minute floor on its monitors.

payload.description: Request body, sent as-is. Only meaningful for POST.

look_for_string.description: The check fails if this string is absent from the response body.

fail_for_string.description: The check fails if this string is present in the response body.

interval_minutes.description: Requested interval. The prober clamps this up to the tenant's minimum_interval_minutes, and up to 60 for a hibernating site, and reports the clamp in the next delivery.

critical.description: A site is 'down' — for the heartbeat site rule and the emergency rule — when a critical monitor is down. Non-critical monitors still record checks and open their own incidents.

heartbeat.description: A signal the site sends to the prober rather than one the prober goes and fetches. The two kinds are judged differently: a heartbeat is late when nothing arrives inside interval + grace, an event is late when a start is not followed by a finish inside timeout.
